content.intro: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. In this lesson, focus on atomic file replacement; then compare it with partial-write handling. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use designing reliable file-based workflows when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. For designing reliable file-based workflows, begin with atomic file replacement. Also distinguish partial-write handling; file cleanup; backups and recovery. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Atomic file replacement
items.text: Check the operation result, use a known storage boundary, and consider empty files, permissions, invalid paths, and cleanup.

items.text: Know when to use partial-write handling, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: When to introduce a database or object-storage service
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Designing Reliable File-Based Workflows
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Check file-operation results and permissions, keep paths inside intended storage areas, and validate uploads before storing them.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring a failed read or write.
common_mistakes.why: Partial or missing data can be mistaken for successful completion.
common_mistakes.fix: Check return values and throw or report a controlled error when required.

common_mistakes.why: Paths can escape the intended directory.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a controlled storage root and reject paths outside it.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting an uploaded filename or extension.
common_mistakes.why: Names and client-provided content types can be forged.
common_mistakes.fix: Generate storage names, enforce size/type policy, and isolate uploaded files.
